policy.purpose: held-out experimental localization benchmark after model parameter selection
policy.prediction_blinding: experimental contact labels are unavailable to the predictor and are read only after raw InterfaceScout predictions have been saved
policy.primary_inclusion: folded full proteins interacting with real material surfaces or nanoparticles with direct experimental protein-side localization and an interpretable native/folded structural model
policy.secondary_inclusion: direct experimental localization is available, but adsorption-induced structural change or structural-model mismatch makes native-PDB localization less clean
excluded_from_primary: systems dominated by major unfolding when a native-PDB contact comparison is not interpretable

cases.evidence: limited proteolysis plus mass spectrometry; Domain II was identified as the silica-facing region
cases.journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
cases.notes: Broad domain-level ground truth; intended for regional rather than exact-residue scoring.

cases.evidence: EDC cross-linking coupled with MALDI-MS identified three HSA peptides adjacent to PAA-coated Fe3O4 nanoparticles; the study mapped the peptides on PDB 2VUF
cases.notes: HSA was adsorbed overnight in deionized water; pH 6.2 is the MES cross-linking/capture condition. The pH-specific InterfaceScout comparison therefore represents the capture condition and is interpreted with this limitation. CD showed negligible secondary-structure change after adsorption.

cases.evidence: site-directed fluorescent labeling/orientation experiment identified the region around position 10 as a dominant silica-contact anchor at pH 6.3
cases.notes: Anchor-level rather than complete-contact-set ground truth.

cases.evidence: site-directed fluorescent labeling/orientation experiment showed increased contribution of the region around position 37 at higher pH
cases.notes: Same protein as the pH 6.3 condition; counted once in unique-protein summaries.

cases.evidence: solution NMR chemical-shift perturbation localized the AuNP interaction site to the Q2-I3 and L15-E18 surface regions
cases.notes: Residue-level NMR localization; replaces the previously considered GB3 case.

cases.evidence: 15N NMR chemical-shift perturbations on MPA-AuNPs localized the preferential interaction to the N-terminal/BC-loop/DE-loop surface region
cases.notes: NMR samples were prepared in 50 mM HEPES at pH 7. MPA-AuNPs were the condition in which beta2m remained essentially stably dissolved; strongly unfolding MHA-AuNP conditions are excluded.

cases.evidence: solid-state NMR chemical-shift perturbation identified the largest perturbations in the Ala250-Lys310 negatively charged surface region while preserving the folded tetramer
cases.notes: 3ECA is the structure used by the experimental study. The homotetramer is retained. Equivalent-subunit scoring accepts the experimentally mapped residue-number region on any symmetry-equivalent chain rather than requiring all four subunits to contact simultaneously.

cases.evidence: limited proteolysis plus LC-MS/MS showed reduced accessibility in residues 140-160 and 480-500 on PS nanoparticles
cases.notes: The experimental paper maps affected peptides onto PDB 1SUV; chains C and E are the N- and C-lobes of one transferrin molecule. This is secondary because 1SUV is a 7.5-A receptor-bound structural model and adsorption also alters transferrin structure.

cases.evidence: limited proteolysis with trypsin/chymotrypsin plus LC-MS/MS showed decreased accessibility in residues 350-380 on PS nanoparticles
cases.notes: The experimental paper maps the affected region on the 1TGU tetramer. Equivalent-subunit scoring is used. This is secondary because additional regions became more accessible and catalase activity changed, indicating adsorption-induced structural perturbation.

pending_or_excluded.reason: high-quality region/domain evidence exists for alphaC versus D/E region engagement on hydrophilic/hydrophobic surfaces, but a chain/domain-aware scorer and defensible mapping from the experimental surface chemistry to an InterfaceScout channel are required before scoring
experimental evidence is primarily molecular-face/orientation level and should not be forced into residue-overlap metrics
AAL/MS studies provide high-resolution adsorption orientation, but the exact residue-level ground-truth list must be extracted and frozen before blind scoring
residue-level adsorption mapping exists, but substantial adsorption-induced unfolding/activity loss complicates a native-PDB primary benchmark
oxidative footprinting identifies two silica adsorption sites, but the adsorbed state shows a large loss of alpha-helical structure, weakening native-PDB interpretation

NMR/proteomics directly identifies a two-alpha-helix silica interface, but the exact adsorption-condition pH and residue-boundary mapping should be frozen from the primary/SI before running the blinded predictor
experimental MS footprinting on MPA-AuNPs is high quality, but the exact experimental residue list must be extracted independently of the simulation results before blind scoring
